claims: A shipped unit the config does not take, named by a synced file, is reported by apply and check, with the file that names it.
A unit added to dev-tools since the last sync is reported until the next apply.
declined in .devtools.toml silences a unit for good; a workflow folder the project takes nothing from is never reported.
check run from a dev-tools checkout, or with --source, says how many files an apply would update; check --receipt-only is the old check.
Every new line is a note with exit 0; check --strict exits 5 when there is anything to report; drift still exits 1; exits 0 to 4 keep their meaning, and no existing test was edited.

A checkout only behind its upstream delivers the upstream commit's files and is not changed; one with work of its own, a detached HEAD or tag, or no upstream is delivered as it is; --as-is skips the fetch; these lines go to standard error only.
